Census: rows of length <=14 whose trace is periodic (p<=16) from t=48 to t=160.

findings.title: Die-crack lemma: a periodic stretch in the trace of a width-W row breaks within f(W) steps
findings.claim: Question: is there an explicit f with f(W) finite such that, for every nonzero finite row of width W in the moving frame (c=0), every stretch of the center trace that is periodic with period p has length at most f(W) (allowing f to depend on p too)? If yes, Problem 1 follows: an eventually periodic seed column makes the row Phi^T(1), of width 2T+1, carry an infinite periodic stretch.
findings.scope: Moving frame Phi(a)=a XOR ((a<<1)|(a<<2)), observation Phi^u(a)[u]. Rows with bit 0 and top bit black. Measured for L<=15, p<=16, trace length 8L+64.
findings.result: Measured, not proved. No row of length <=14 has a trace periodic (p<=16) from t=48 to t=160. The longest periodic stretch R(L) over all rows of length L goes 12,12,10,13,14,14,14,15,18,18,24,18,23,23 for L=2..15: roughly L+8, slightly under a random-sequence baseline. Nothing hints at a row whose stretch grows with trace length.
limitations: Bounded search; the observed R(L) can be matched by pure counting (2^L rows x N windows), so the data do not separate a real mechanism from chance.
f(W) for the seed row only needs to hold for rows of the form Phi^T(1); the general lemma may be strictly harder than Problem 1.
c=0 only; other observation offsets are rows shifted against the frame and were not run.
Trace length 8L+64 caps detectable stretches; rows whose periodic stretch starts late are under-sampled.
findings.next_action: 1) Extend to L<=24 with traces to 64L in C, recording the argmax rows. 2) If R(L) stays near L+c, look at the argmax rows for the mechanism that ends each stretch (the coin analog: a die crack reaching the field). Candidate: the left-edge information of the row crosses the observed column after about W steps (Rule 30 is left-permutive), and a left-permutive update cannot keep an XOR-injected defect out of a periodic column. 3) Try to state that as a Lean lemma for p=1 first (constant stretches), where the bound should be easiest.
